Subject: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) - Hosted vs Current Provider (call recap)

Hi Alex -- thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we need to qualify to scope a hosted pilot and pricing:

Summary of what we heard from you on the call:
- Primary workload: customer-facing chat (streaming) + some async batch scoring endpoints for recommendations.
- Concurrency: peak ~200 concurrent active users (mostly chat), sustained 60-80 RPS across all endpoints.
- Typical request size: 30-120 tokens in, 50-300 tokens generated per response (chat).
- Current provider (internal) end-to-end SLOs you observe: p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.2s (this includes network + app + provider inference).

Open items we want to validate to complete the qualification:
1) Confirm the end-to-end p95 and p99 targets you need for hosted API versus what you currently get (we captured the numbers above - please confirm).
2) For streaming chat, do you require byte-by-byte streaming or can you accept chunked (sentence/segment) streaming?
3) Any hard limits for tail latency during peak bursts (e.g., p99 must be <2s under 95th-percentile traffic)?
4) Will FinLytics allow a short benchmark window (3 business days) against a subset of production traffic or a realistic replay? We will provide a time-limited API key and test harness.

Next steps I propose:
- Alex confirms the p95/p99 numbers and streaming requirement by EOD tomorrow.
- We run a 3-day benchmark on Redwood hosted with identical request mix.
- SE (Rishi) to coordinate quota and tokenization checks and collect sample payloads.
- I'll send SLA comparison and a short mutual action plan after we have the numbers.

Attaching a draft SLA comparison and a sample payload file so Rishi can review while we wait for Alex's confirmation.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa -- thanks for the recap. Confirming the numbers from our side and adding a few clarifications:

- Current observed end-to-end: p95 = ~450ms, p99 = ~1.2s. These numbers include our frontend, auth, and current provider RTT.
- Target for any replacement: p95 <= 500ms, p99 <= 1.5s end-to-end. We can be flexible on p99 during the benchmark but would like to see steady-state results within those thresholds.
- Streaming: we need low-latency streaming for the chat product. Per-byte streaming is preferred for immediate token echoing, but chunked/sentence streaming is acceptable as long as per-chunk delay stays low (<200ms typical).
- Concurrency: peak 200 concurrent chat users; concurrent model requests translate to ~40-60 simultaneous inference calls at peak (clients multiplex).
- Payloads: sample-payloads.json attached to your email looks representative. We can provide a replay of 24 hours of anonymized traffic if needed, but prefer to start with the sample replay then escalate if needed.

We're open to the 3-day benchmark. Please also include any recommendations for request batching/limits you expect from Redwood so we can instrument our clients.

Best,

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) - Hosted vs Current Provider

Thanks Alex -- helpful context. A few quick technical clarifications from the SE side so our benchmark is aligned:

1) End-to-end definition: we will measure from the client POST to the completion of the final token (inclusive) when testing non-streaming. For streaming tests we'll measure first-byte and per-chunk latencies as separate metrics. Please confirm if your current numbers (p95/p99) use a similar measurement point.

2) Tokenization: which tokenizer do you use in production? We need to ensure token counts in the replay match the model tokenizer we pick. If you can confirm model and tokenizer (or allow us to run tokenization locally against sample payloads), that helps.

3) Burst behavior: how long do your concurrent peaks last (minutes/hours)? For planning, we need to know whether we should stress test short spikes (1-5 min) vs extended peaks (30+ min).

4) TLS + network hop: is FinLytics routing via a CDN/edge that adds extra RTT? If so, please share an egress IP range we can mirror in the benchmark.

Regarding hosted capabilities: preliminary note -- Redwood hosted supports streaming with per-chunk latencies typically in the 40-80ms range for the model families FinLytics is looking at (with no additional app-layer queuing). However, end-to-end numbers will depend on client network RTT, application middleware, and whether you enable client-side prefix caching/batching. We'll instrument the benchmark to show p50/p95/p99 for first-byte, per-chunk, and final-complete times.

If you confirm tokenization and burst patterns, I'll prepare a benchmark harness and request a short access key for FinLytics.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
